doc.title: John Budd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [transcript only]

title: Pay and hours at the silent-film theatre, 1926
summary: Thirty dollars a week for five hours a day; the work made him agile at the piano.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: And when the boy struck it rich, some rich guy up in New York came around and gave him ten dollars a week and that was big money. And so I said to Mr. Acker, I didn’t like to be presumptuous, but Mr. Acker, how much do you pay? I thought if he said ten dollars a week I might ask for fifteen. He said “we pay thirty dollars a week.” That was big money in 1926. And he said “we have union scale, it’s a dollar an hour, but we don’t have a union but we pay it. And you play five hours a day.” I played the off hours when not many people would be there listening, from one to three, the regular guy from three to five, I played five to seven, and the other man seven to nine, I played nine to ten, and he played ten to eleven. So it was five hours a day, six days week, at a dollar an hour is thirty dollars week. And that was the end of that.
Well if you play some five hours a day for three months you have to get better. So I became fairly agile at playing the piano.
